mainTopic: The sealed-ring and hole-less-needle rules for women, and the ban on a man going out on שבת in a spiked sandal (סנדל המסומר).
overview: This amud joins the sugya in the middle of a contradiction about a woman's ring with a seal. The ברייתא of רבי נחמיה finishes: he judges a vessel by its working part, while the חכמים judge it by its supporting structure (הַמַּעֲמִיד). רבא and then רב נחמן בר יצחק give two more ways to settle the contradiction. רבא says a sealed ring is a man's ornament and a plain ring is a woman's ornament. רב נחמן בר יצחק says טומאה and שבת use different tests: 'working vessel' for one, and ornament versus משוי for the other. Next the גמרא asks what a needle without a hole is used for. רב יוסף's answer, that it gathers the hair, is challenged by אביי, so רב אדא explains that it parts the hair, and רבא adds that on שבת it is worn as jewelry with a gold plate. A new משנה then lists items a man may not go out with on שבת, starting with a spiked sandal (סנדל המסומר). The גמרא explains that ban through stories of a deadly panic that spiked sandals caused, and it says the decree is limited to שבת because the tragedy happened on שבת. It then asks why יום טוב is not permitted as well, and the משנה it quotes continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: a vessel's status follows its working part
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with רבי נחמיה's examples. A vessel's legal status is set by the part that does the actual job: the nails of a hanging board, the rungs of a ladder, the chains of a scale.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a hanging board, follow its nails. With a ladder, follow its rungs. With a large scale, follow its chains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that shows רבי נחמיה's general rule. A vessel's legal status depends on the part that does the work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a hanging board, the nails are what actually hold things up. For a ladder, it is the rungs you climb on. For a scale, it is the chains that hold the pans. So רבי נחמיה judges a vessel by its functional part. For a ring, that means the seal (חותם) is the main part, and this supports reading our משנה as following רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: A hanging board or peg-rack for hanging items
Follow / go by, meaning 'its status is determined by'
A large scale or balance (some say a bed frame)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a ברייתא that began on the previous עמוד. These lines are רבי נחמיה's view, used as support for the earlier answer to the contradiction. They are not a brand-new topic.

phrases.english: With a hanging board, follow its nails.
phrases.notes: The nails hold the hanging items, so they do the real work.

phrases.english: With a ladder, follow its rungs.
phrases.notes: The rungs are what you climb on.

phrases.english: With a large scale, follow its chains.
phrases.notes: Not its base, but the chains that hold the pans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד, which supports the first answer that our משנה follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה, which treats a sealed ring differently, follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי נחמיה says a vessel's status follows its functional part.

steps.title: The חכמים: everything follows the supporting structure
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי נחמיה. A vessel's status is set by its main structure (הַמַּעֲמִיד), not by its working attachment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: everything follows the supporting part.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposing view of the חכמים. A vessel is judged by its main body or support, not by the functional add-on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a ring, the body of the ring is the main thing, not the seal. So according to the חכמים, a sealed ring and a plain ring are basically the same ring. That fits the משנה in כלים, which treats them the same. Our משנה, which treats a sealed ring differently, must then follow רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: The supporting structure, the part that holds the vessel up

steps.whatToRemember: The first answer: our משנה follows רבי נחמיה, for whom the seal is the main part of the ring. The משנה in כלים follows the חכמים, for whom the ring body is the main part.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Everything follows the supporting part.
phrases.notes: The main structure determines the vessel's status.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַמַּעֲמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי נחמיה inside the same ברייתא, which completes the first answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a vessel's status follows its supporting structure, not its functional attachment.

steps.title: רבא: each ring is an ornament for a different person
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. The משנה in כלים speaks 'לצדדים', about two different cases. A sealed ring is a man's ornament, and a plain ring is a woman's ornament.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It teaches disjunctively. If it has a seal, it is a man's ornament. If it has no seal, it is a woman's ornament.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second way to settle the contradiction. He explains that the משנה in כלים is describing two separate cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in כלים says both rings can become טמא. רבא explains that each one is an ornament for a different person: the sealed ring for a man, the plain ring for a woman. So a woman wearing a sealed ring is wearing something that is not her ornament. That is why our משנה forbids it on שבת. No disagreement between תנאים is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches 'to the sides', meaning it lists two separate cases
An ornament or piece of jewelry

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a sealed ring is never an ornament. It is a man's ornament. For a woman, it is not her ornament, so on שבת it counts as carrying.

phrases.english: Rava said: It teaches disjunctively (two separate cases):
If it has a seal on it, it is a man's ornament;
If it has no seal on it, it is a woman's ornament.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the contradiction that steps 1 and 2 resolved by citing רבי נחמיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The contradiction between our משנה and the משנה in כלים about sealed rings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in כלים seemed to say that both rings are ornaments for the same person, a woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ring is an ornament for a different person: sealed for a man, plain for a woman. So for a woman, a sealed ring is not an ornament.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: טומאה and שבת use different tests
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the contradiction was never real. For טומאה the test is whether the item is a working vessel (כלי מעשה). For שבת the test is whether it is an ornament or a burden (משוי).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Are you comparing טומאה to שבת? For טומאה, the תורה said 'a working vessel', and a ring with a seal is a vessel. For שבת, the תורה forbade because of carrying a burden. With no seal, it is an ornament. With a seal, it is a burden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a third answer. He rejects the comparison itself, because טומאה and שבת are judged by completely different standards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item can become טמא if it is a functional vessel. A sealed ring is useful for stamping, so it clearly qualifies. On שבת the question is different: is she wearing jewelry, or carrying a load? A plain ring is jewelry. A sealed ring is a tool that is not her jewelry, so it counts as a משוי.

keyTerms.meaning: You are raising a contradiction (comparing two sources)
A working vessel, the Torah's test for susceptibility to טומאה
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
A burden, an item that counts as carrying on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to the sealed-ring contradiction. (1) It is a dispute: our משנה follows רבי נחמיה. (2) רבא: each ring is an ornament for a different person. (3) רב נחמן בר יצחק: טומאה tests 'vessel', while שבת tests 'ornament versus burden'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a key method in learning. The same object can be judged differently in different areas of הלכה, because each area has its own Torah-based test.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Are you raising a contradiction from impurity to Shabbat?!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; he's saying you can't compare these two.

phrases.english: Regarding impurity, the Torah said 'a working vessel',
phrases.notes: Based on במדבר לא:נא.

phrases.english: and it (a sealed ring) is a vessel.
Regarding Shabbat, the Torah forbade because of a burden;
if it has no seal on it, it is an ornament;
if it has a seal on it, it is a burden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer, which removes the contradiction entirely instead of re-reading either משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The contradiction between our משנה and the משנה in כלים about sealed rings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between areas of law (different criteria)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If both rings can become טמא, then both should be treated the same on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאה depends on being a working vessel, while שבת depends on ornament versus burden. A sealed ring is a vessel, but for a woman it is a burden.

steps.title: Next item in the משנה: a needle without a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on to the next ruling in the משנה: a woman may not go out on שבת with a needle that has no hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: Nor with a needle that is not perforated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line in the משנה. This step is a setup for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A needle without a hole cannot be used for sewing. So it seems strange that the משנה even mentions it. Quoting this line prepares the question of what such a needle is used for.

phrases.english: Nor with a needle that is not perforated.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the sealed-ring topic and quotes the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may not go out on שבת with a needle that has no hole.

steps.title: What is a hole-less needle used for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what use a needle without a hole could have, since it cannot sew.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it suited?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real clarifying question: what is this kind of needle good for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only lists items a woman might actually wear or use. If a hole-less needle has no use, why would anyone go out with it? The גמרא needs to know its function to understand the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: For what is it fit? What is it used for?

phrases.english: For what is it suited?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה line quoted in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical use a needle without a hole has.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a woman uses it to hold her hair
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that a woman uses a hole-less needle to gather and pin up her hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Because a woman gathers her hair with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. Women use this needle as a hairpin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it is a real item that women use, a woman might go out wearing it in her hair, which explains why the משנה bothers to mention it. But on this reading the needle sits fixed in her hair, and the next step (אביי) challenges whether such an item should be forbidden at all.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Since a woman gathers her hair with it.
phrases.notes: She uses it like a hairpin to hold her hair in place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הוֹאִיל וְאִשָּׁה אוֹגֶרֶת בָּהּ שְׂעָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hole-less needle is used by women to gather and pin up their hair.

steps.title: אביי challenges רב יוסף with the pure garter
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if the needle holds up her hair, it should be permitted, just like a pure garter.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, let the needle be like a pure garter, and let it be permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer from Step 7. If the needle holds her hair in place, it should be allowed, just like a בירית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman may go out with a בירית because she will never take it off in public, so there is no worry she will carry it. The same should be true of a hair-pin: removing it would let her hair fall loose in the street, so she will not take it out. Under רב יוסף's explanation, then, the ban on the needle makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: A garter, a strap that holds up stockings
Ritually pure, meaning it cannot become טמא

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Then let it be like a ritually pure garter,
phrases.notes: A garter is allowed on שבת because a woman will not remove it in public.

phrases.english: and let it be permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְתֶהֱוֵי כְּבִירִית טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the needle is used to gather the hair
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A worn item that she will never remove in public, like a בירית, is permitted. A hair-pin fits that same pattern, so it should also be permitted, yet the משנה forbids it.

steps.title: רב אדא gives a new reason: the needle parts her hair
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא נרשאה explains that the needle is a tool for parting hair, so she might take it out and carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אדא of Naresh explained it before רב יוסף: the reason is that a woman parts her hair with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא tells us the earlier explanation is dropped. רב אדא נרשאה offers a new reason for the ban: the needle is a hair-parting tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A parting tool is not something fixed in place like a garter. It is a utensil that she takes out and uses. Because she may remove it in the street to fix her hair and then carry it, it is forbidden. This answers אביי's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which drops the previous explanation

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Adda of Naresh explained it
before Rav Yosef:
Since a woman parts her hair with it.
phrases.notes: Because it is a working tool, she may take it out and carry it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב אַדָּא נַרְשָׁאָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's explanation after אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of what the item is used for
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The needle holds her hair in place, so it is like a garter and should be permitted
steps.terutzMaskana: The needle is a hair-parting tool that she takes out and uses, so there is a real worry she will carry it

steps.title: What use is the needle on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a woman would wear the needle on שבת at all, since parting hair is not done then.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת, what is it good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question on רב אדא's answer: if the needle is for parting hair, why would she wear it on שבת? This sets up רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combing and parting hair is not done on שבת. If the needle has no use that day, there is no reason she would wear it. In that case there would be no need to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: For what is it suited, meaning what is it good for

phrases.english: On Shabbat, what is it good for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רב אדא's explanation applies on שבת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a woman would wear a hair-parting needle on שבת

steps.title: רבא: the needle has a gold plate worn as an ornament
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the needle has a gold plate on its end. On שבת she wears it with the plate on her forehead as jewelry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It has a gold plate on its end. On weekdays she parts her hair with it. On שבת she places it so the plate rests against her forehead.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 10. On שבת the needle serves as jewelry because of the gold plate on its end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because she wears it as an ornament, she does go out with it on שבת. It is still a weekday tool for parting hair, though, so she might take it out and carry it. That is why the משנה forbids it.
steps.whatToRemember: The hole-less needle is forbidden because it is a hair-parting tool, not a fixed item like a garter. On שבת she wears it as jewelry with its gold plate on her forehead, so the worry that she will remove and carry it is real.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: טַס שֶׁל זָהָב יֵשׁ לָהּ עַל רֹאשָׁהּ.
phrases.english: It has a gold plate on its end.
On a weekday, she parts her hair with it;
on Shabbat, she places it against her forehead.
phrases.notes: She wears it as an ornament.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: טַס שֶׁל זָהָב יֵשׁ לָהּ עַל רֹאשָׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The needle has a gold plate. On שבת it is worn as jewelry on the forehead, so she goes out with it, and since it is a tool she might remove and carry it.

steps.title: New משנה: items a man may not go out with on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists items a man may not go out wearing on שבת: a spiked sandal, a single sandal, תפילין, an unproven amulet, armor, a helmet and leg-guards. If he does, he is not liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man may not go out with a spiked sandal. He may not go out with a single sandal unless he has a wound on his foot. He may not go out with תפילין, or with an amulet that is not from an expert. He may not go out with armor, a helmet, or metal leg-guards. If he did go out, he is not liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Until now the topic was women. Now it lists things a man may not wear outside on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these items are worn, not carried in the hand, so wearing them outside is not real Torah-level carrying. That is why he is not liable to bring a חטאת. The prohibition is a rabbinic safeguard. The גמרא will explain the reason for each item.

keyTerms.meaning: A single sandal, only one shoe
An expert whose amulets have proven effective
A sin-offering, brought for an accidental Torah-level violation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these items are allowed just because there is no חטאת. They are still forbidden. The phrase only means the violation is not on the level of Torah-level carrying.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A man may not go out
with a nail-studded sandal.
Nor with a single sandal,
when there is no wound on his foot.
Nor with phylacteries,
nor with an amulet
when it is not from an expert.
Nor with armor, nor with a helmet,
nor with metal leg-guards.
And if he went out, he is not liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יֵצֵא הָאִישׁ בְּסַנְדָּל הַמְסוּמָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about men after finishing the women's items
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man may not go out on שבת with a spiked sandal, a single sandal (unless his foot is wounded), תפילין, an unproven amulet, armor, a helmet or leg-guards. If he does, he is not liable to bring a חטאת.

steps.title: Why is the spiked sandal forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the ban on a spiked sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A spiked sandal: what is the reason it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the new משנה with its first item. This question sets up the explanation that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sandal is ordinary clothing, and the nails are part of the shoe, so there seems to be no carrying problem. The גמרא therefore needs a special reason for this ban.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A spiked sandal: what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the new משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the rabbinic ban on going out with a spiked sandal on שבת

steps.title: שמואל: A reversed spiked sandal caused a deadly panic in a cave
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains the ban on the סנדל המסומר through a story. Jews hiding in a cave saw a reversed sandal print, thought someone had gone out and been seen, and crushed each other to death in the panic.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: They were survivors of the religious persecution, and they were hiding in a cave. They said: whoever wants to come in may come in, but whoever wants to go out may not go out. The sandal of one of them got turned around. They thought one of them had gone out, the enemies had seen him, and now the enemies were coming upon them. They pushed against one another and killed one another, more than the enemies had killed among them.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question from Step 13. He explains the ban on the spiked sandal by telling the story of a disaster it caused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hiders had a strict rule that nobody may leave, because leaving could reveal the hiding place. A reversed spiked sandal left prints that looked like someone walking out. In the panic and crush, more Jews died at each other's hands than at the enemy's hands, so the רבנן banned this sandal on שבת as a reminder of the tragedy.

keyTerms.meaning: Survivors who escaped the decrees of religious persecution
His sandal got turned around (front became back)
They pushed and crushed against one another

steps.confusionAlert: The ban here does not come from the normal מלאכה of carrying. A shoe counts as clothing, not as something carried. The ban is a special גזירה made because of a historical tragedy linked to this kind of sandal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה in Step 12 lists the spiked sandal among the banned items, even though a person normally may wear shoes into רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
They were survivors of the persecution,
and they were hiding in a cave,
and they said: whoever enters may enter,
phrases.notes: Coming in is safe. It does not reveal the hiding place.

phrases.english: but whoever goes out may not go out.
phrases.notes: Someone going out might be seen and give away everyone hiding inside.

phrases.english: The sandal of one of them was turned around,
phrases.notes: Because of the reversed sandal, the spike marks looked like footprints walking out of the cave.

phrases.english: they thought that one of them had gone out
and enemies had seen him
and now they were coming upon them.
They pushed against one another
and killed one another,
more than the enemies had killed among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 13 about the reason for banning the spiked sandal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is going out in a סנדל המסומר on שבת forbidden?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because of a tragedy: a reversed spiked sandal made hiders think they had been discovered, and they killed each other in the panic.

steps.title: רבי אילעאי בן אלעזר: They heard the sandal's sound above the cave
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעאי בן אלעזר gives a different version of the tragedy. People hiding in a cave heard the noise of spiked sandals above them, thought the enemy had arrived, and crushed each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעאי בן אלעזר says: They were sitting in a cave, and they heard a sound from on top of the cave. They thought the enemies had come upon them. They pushed against one another and killed one another, more than the enemies had killed among them.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage offers a different version of the story behind the ban. This time the panic came from a sound, not from footprints.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending is the same: a deadly crush caused by false fear. The difference is the trigger. Here it was the loud clatter of a spiked sandal heard above the cave, not a misleading footprint. Either way, the spiked sandal is linked to the tragedy, so the ban still makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: They heard a sound (the noise of the spiked sandal)
From on top of the cave

phrases.english: Rabbi Elai ben Elazar says:
They were sitting in a cave,
and they heard a sound from on top of the cave.
phrases.notes: The sound was the clatter of a spiked sandal.

phrases.english: They thought that enemies had come upon them.
They pushed against one another
and killed one another,
more than the enemies had killed among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative version of the event that שמואל described in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is going out in a סנדל המסומר on שבת forbidden?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Hiders in a cave heard spiked sandals above them, panicked, and killed one another.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל: They heard the sound behind a בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל gives a third version. People gathered in a בית הכנסת heard the noise of spiked sandals behind the building, feared an enemy attack, and crushed each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל said: They were sitting in a synagogue, and they heard a sound from behind the synagogue. They thought the enemies had come upon them. They pushed against one another and killed one another, more than the enemies had killed among them.
steps.whatsHappening: A third sage gives yet another version of the same kind of tragedy. Here the place is a בית הכנסת instead of a cave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי אילעאי בן אלעזר, רמי בר יחזקאל says the panic came from hearing the sandal's sound. He changes the location to a בית הכנסת, with the sound coming from behind it. All three versions agree that a spiked sandal caused a deadly crush among Jews.
steps.whatToRemember: All three versions (שמואל, רבי אילעאי בן אלעזר, רמי בר יחזקאל) agree on the law and on the basic event: a spiked sandal set off a panic, and Jews killed more of each other than the enemy did. They differ only on the details. Was it a reversed footprint or a sound? Was it a cave or a בית הכנסת? Because of this tragedy, the רבנן banned going out in a סנדל המסומר on שבת.

phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel said:
They were sitting in a synagogue,
and they heard a sound from behind the synagogue.
They thought that enemies had come upon them.
They pushed against one another
and killed one another,
more than the enemies had killed among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative version, close to Step 15 (a sound caused the panic) but set in a בית הכנסת instead of a cave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is going out in a סנדל המסומר on שבת forbidden?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People in a בית הכנסת heard spiked sandals behind the building, panicked, and killed one another.

steps.title: The decree that came out of the tragedy
steps.stepSummary: Because of the disaster, the חכמים decreed that a person may not go out wearing a סנדל המסומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time they said: A person may not go out wearing a spiked sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story by telling us what the חכמים did about it: they banned going out in a spiked sandal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line connects the stories in Steps 14-16 to the law in the משנה. Whichever version of the tragedy is correct, the result is the same: the ban is a rabbinic decree made to remember the disaster. It is not a ban based on the laws of carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: At that time, meaning right after the tragedy
A person may not go out
A sandal with nails (spikes) in its sole

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ban is a גזירה tied to a historical event. That is why the following steps can ask exactly when the ban applies.

phrases.english: At that time they said:
phrases.notes: Right after the disaster described in the stories.

phrases.english: A person may not go out with a spiked sandal.
phrases.notes: This is the rabbinic decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal result out of the tragedy stories told in Steps 14-16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ban on the סנדל המסומר is a rabbinic decree made because of a tragedy involving spiked sandals.

steps.title: Then why not ban it on weekdays too?
steps.stepSummary: If the ban comes from a tragedy, the spiked sandal should be forbidden every day, not just on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should be forbidden on a weekday as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave. If the sandal caused a disaster, it should be banned on regular days too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the stories as told so far connects the tragedy to שבת. So a decree based on them should apply all the time. Yet the משנה lists the sandal only among the things forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is the reason

phrases.english: If so, on a weekday it should also be prohibited!
phrases.notes: The reason given does not explain why the ban is limited to שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the scope of the decree stated in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ban comes from the tragedy (Steps 14-17)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reason that is not connected to שבת should lead to a ban every day. So why is the ban limited to שבת?

steps.title: The tragedy happened on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The disaster took place on שבת, so the חכמים limited the decree to שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the incident happened, it happened on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the tragedy happened on שבת, so the decree only covers שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer adds a new fact: the event took place on שבת. The חכמים made the decree match the circumstances of the original disaster. That explains why weekdays are not included.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sandal is forbidden because of a carrying problem. The ban is limited to שבת only because that is when the tragedy happened.

phrases.english: When the incident occurred, it was on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: The decree matches the day of the original event.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a historical detail that limits the scope of the decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tragedy had nothing to do with שבת, so the ban should apply every day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tragedy happened on שבת, so the decree was made only for שבת.

steps.title: Then יום טוב should be permitted
steps.stepSummary: If the decree only covers the day the tragedy happened, יום טוב should be allowed. Yet the גמרא is about to quote a source that restricts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then on יום טוב it should be permitted! Why, then, did we learn in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. If the ban is tied to שבת, then יום טוב should be allowed. It is now setting up a quote from a משנה that seems to say otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 19 limited the decree to שבת. Since the tragedy did not happen on יום טוב, the sandal should be permitted then. The words אַלְּמָה תְּנַן introduce a משנה showing that the spiked sandal is restricted on יום טוב as well, and that משנה continues in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: Why, then, did we learn (in a משנה)? It introduces a source that contradicts what was just said.

phrases.english: On a Festival it should be permitted!
phrases.notes: This follows from tying the ban to שבת.

phrases.english: Why, then, did we learn:
phrases.notes: The משנה being quoted here continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 19 by drawing out what it implies for יום טוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the decree is limited to שבת because the tragedy happened on שבת (Step 19)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the decree only covers the day of the event, יום טוב should be permitted. But a משנה (about to be quoted) restricts the spiked sandal on יום טוב too.
